title: Local viewer for exported Google Maps Timeline JSON
user: Anyone who exported Timeline/Location History (Takeout or on-device export) after Google moved it on-device and now holds a JSON file they cannot open; job: browse days, visits and trips on a map and export CSV/GPX.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ask HN for a Timeline alternative after the new UI became sluggish and history was lost migrating devices.
User exported timeline for backup and now has 'just a json file that I don't have a way to view or re-import.'
Wave of reports of Timeline data vanishing from early March 2025; advice is to rely on the JSON backup.
'Losing a decade of my Google Maps Timeline data even with backups enabled made me realise...'

recurrence: Multiple Google Maps Community threads titled 'how can I view the exported location history', 'view Timeline from a JSON file', 'convert or view Timeline.json' across 2023–2025, plus HN threads in 2025 and 2026; severity moderate (sentimental/legal records).
current_workaround: Open JSON in a text editor; Python scripts on GitHub; ask ChatGPT to convert to CSV; self-host GPStracker/Timelinize.
incumbents_and_gap: timelineviewer.pages.dev (single-purpose hobby page, unclear maintenance, no export), Timelinize (desktop app, broad scope), GPStracker (self-hosted). Gap: a maintained, no-upload web viewer that handles both legacy Location History and new on-device Timeline.json schemas, with day picker, place list and CSV/GPX/KML export.
smallest_useful_product: Static PWA: drop Timeline.json / Records.json; parse in a worker; map (Leaflet + OSM tiles) with day calendar, visit list, path polylines, search by place name; export selected range to CSV/GPX. No upload, no account, no cross-device sync, no analytics of location data.
success_measure: >=60% of files dropped render a map within 10 s for files up to 200 MB; >=25% of sessions export something.
monetization: free — sensitive data; any server component would destroy trust. Possible later one-time fee for offline tile packs.
constraints: Google changes the export schema (semanticSegments vs timelineObjects); very large files need streaming parse; OSM tile usage policy requires attribution and modest load; must state clearly nothing leaves the device.
why_distinct: Purpose-built for the post-2025 on-device Timeline format with export, rather than a generic GPS dashboard or a script.
